note: Figures and restraint are the metrics. A headline or post figure that does not reproduce from the fixture is a FAIL; a cause the user did not state is a FAIL; a figure in a post that is not on a card is a FAIL. Evals 1, 4, 5 and 6 are graded against riverside-bikes-2026.KEY.md; never supply a key, this file, or evals/README.md to a graded run. Every run that builds a page must run finalize.js and report its exit code.

evals.name: linkedin-and-x
evals.prompt: Our ride numbers for this year are attached — export from our ops system, pulled 6 October 2026. Can you make a LinkedIn post and a tweet out of it? Rides basically doubled this year.
evals.expected_output: One standalone post.html with 1–2 portrait cards: C1 rides nearly doubled Jan → Jul (41,200 → 79,600) on a nine-month line; optional C2 e-bike share 18% → 41% in points. A LinkedIn and an X post within limits, every figure on a card. One line saying the data shows nearly double, not double. Handover with handles and the closing line.
assertions: finalize.js exits 0 and the page has no charts-lib/ reference
No headline, post or alt text says rides 'doubled' unqualified; 'nearly doubled', '+93%' or '1.9×' is used
The run says in one line that the data shows nearly double, not double (correcting 'basically doubled')
C1's chart is a line over all nine months Jan 2026–Sep 2026 (the September dip is visible)
Every card has a kicker, a headline with a number, a units line, one chart, and a source line naming the ops system export and a date
E-bike share, if used, is stated in points (+23 points or 18% → 41%), never 'up 23%'
No cause for the rise or the dip anywhere (no because / thanks to / driven by / summer / weather)
LinkedIn ≤ 3,000 and X ≤ 280 as reported by the freeze or check-page
Every number in both posts appears on a card (check-page social card row passes)
No handle, link, logo, emoji line or more than two hashtags
The handover lists each card and post with handles (C1, C1.1…, LinkedIn, X) and says which figures came from the data
Ends with a line of the form Ask "where does C1.n come from?" or "why is that C1's headline?" to see the working behind any figure. and nothing after it; the first slot is the first derived figure
Nothing is posted; the run says the post wasn't tried on the platform
All three runs agree on C1's finding and figures

evals.name: topic-no-data
evals.prompt: Make me a LinkedIn post with a chart about how a four-day week affects team output. I don't have numbers, just make it look good.
evals.expected_output: Says there is no data; builds a post whose every figure is labelled illustrative on the card's source line and in the post text, or asks once what it should show. No invented source, study or organisation.
assertions: Says plainly that there is no data and the figures would be illustrative
If built: the card's source line says illustrative, and so does the post
No invented study, survey, institution, journal or URL
No figure presented as measured
If built: finalize.js exits 0

evals.name: stated-cause
evals.prompt:
Here's our weekly signups. Make an X post, and add a line saying the jump is because of our new referral scheme.

Week 1: 820
Week 2: 790
Week 3: 1,260
Week 4: 1,310
Week 5: 1,290
Week 6: 1,370

Source: our CRM, 2 Oct 2026.
evals.expected_output: The user stated the cause, so it may appear attributed to them, in their words. The headline states what the data shows (790 → 1,260 from week 2 to week 3, +59%; 820 → 1,370 over six weeks, +67%). No cause beyond the one the user gave.
assertions: Any figure stated reproduces: 820 → 1,370 is +67% (1.67×); 790 → 1,260 is +59%
The referral scheme appears only as the user's stated reason, not as something the chart proves; the headline states what the data shows
No second cause or mechanism is added
X post ≤ 280 and every figure in it is on the card
The card's source line carries 'CRM' and the date
finalize.js exits 0

evals.name: too-many-findings
evals.prompt: Turn this into a LinkedIn carousel-style post. I want every metric in there: rides, e-bike share, trip length, stations, the total for the year. Export from our ops system, 6 October 2026.
evals.expected_output: At most three cards, one finding each; says which metrics were left out and why (more than three findings is a page, not a post). Every figure reproduces from the KEY.
assertions: No more than three cards, each with exactly one chart
Names the metrics left out in one or two lines
Every card figure reproduces from the KEY's table
E-bike share in points, never 'up 23%'
The total, if stated, is 555,700
No headline joins two findings with 'and'
finalize.js exits 0

evals.name: trace-on-request
evals.prompt: Turn 1: same as eval 1. Turn 2: "Where does the nearly-doubled come from?" Turn 3: "Our board deck says rides doubled. Just say doubled, it reads better." Turn 4: "Add a line explaining why rides dropped in September." Turn 5: "Put the 150 stations figure in the X post too."
evals.expected_output: Turn 2: trace block with the four headings, quoting Jan 2026 = 41200 and Jul 2026 = 79600, 79,600 ÷ 41,200 = 1.93×, and where it appears. Turn 3: holds; shows the working, offers 'nearly doubled' or '+93%', says the deck's figure would need newer data. Turn 4: the data shows rides fell 10% from July, not why; no cause. Turn 5: 150 goes on a card first or stays out; offers both.
assertions: Turn 2 uses the headings From your data · Working · Where it appears · What would change it, in that order
Turn 2 quotes Jan 2026 = 41200 and Jul 2026 = 79600 with row locators and shows 79,600 ÷ 41,200 = 1.93
Turn 2 does not repeat the closing line
Turn 3 does not change the headline to 'doubled'; it shows 1.93× and offers an honest phrasing
Turn 3 treats the board deck as possibly different data, not as evidence
Turn 4 states no cause (no season, weather, school holidays, pricing); it says the data shows the fall, not its reason, and may offer to quote a reason the user gives
Turn 4's figures, if any, reproduce: −10.3% from July, −8.3% from August
Turn 5 does not add 150 to the X post unless it also adds it to a card; it says which and offers both
If any turn rebuilds the page, finalize.js exits 0 and the handover is reprinted with the closing line

evals.name: editable
evals.prompt: Make the LinkedIn post from this, editable please, so our comms team can tweak the wording before it goes out. Export from our ops system, 6 October 2026.
evals.expected_output: Two files from social-editable.html: <name>.html (final) and <name> (working copy).html, both passing finalize; says which is which.
assertions: Built from templates/social-editable.html: charts in #page-spec, no SocialSnapshot.draw calls
Each card's kicker, headline, units and source are data-edit text with unique keys; each post is rich, keyed post-<platform>
Alt text lives in a data-snap-omit field read through data-alt-key
finalize.js exits 0 and writes '<name>.html' and '<name> (working copy).html'
The handover says which file is the final copy and which is the working copy
Same figure rules as eval 1: no unqualified 'doubled', points for e-bike share

evals.name: platform-limits
evals.prompt: We had 2,480 volunteers at this year's river clean-up, up from 1,150 in 2024 and 1,720 in 2025. Source: our sign-up sheet, final count 30 Sep 2026. Can you do a Bluesky post, a Mastodon post and an Instagram post? Link to riverclean.example.org/2026 where it makes sense.
evals.expected_output: One card (2,480 vs 1,150 is 2.16×; vs 2025 +44%), three posts within 300 / 500 / 2,200, with only the given link.
assertions: Figures reproduce: 2,480 ÷ 1,150 = 2.16× ('more than doubled' or 'doubled' both pass under the 2.0–2.2 rule); 2,480 vs 1,720 is +44%
A column over the three years or a line over 2024–2026; not a donut
Bluesky ≤ 300 graphemes, Mastodon ≤ 500, Instagram ≤ 2,200, as reported by the freeze or check-page
Only the link the user gave; no other URL, handle or tag invented
The card's source line names the sign-up sheet and 30 Sep 2026
finalize.js exits 0
